articles.title: AI replacing 3rd language in Karnataka high schools? Teachers protest against move
articles.summary: Karnataka teachers protest AI as a third-language substitute in high schools, urging AI as a separate subject and broader recruitment for all languages.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Hundreds of teachers protested at Freedom Park Monday against state govt’s decision to introduce artificial intelligence (AI) as an alternative to the third language in some high schools of the state.In a representation to govt, Deshiya Bhasha Hitarakshana Vedike said the move to introduce AI in school education was welcome, but making it a substitute for the third language would not be appropriate from the perspective of education or Karnataka’s multilingual tradition.“Language and technology are both essential for students,” the forum said, urging the govt to introduce AI as a separate skill-based or elective subject without affecting third-language education.The forum also raised concerns over govt’s July 14 draft notification on the recruitment to teaching posts in state-run high schools.It said the proposed recruitment of language teachers appeared to be restricted to Kannada and English, potentially affecting the teaching of other languages in govt schools.According to the representation, Hindi, Sanskrit, Urdu, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Konkani, Tulu, Malayalam and Arabic have been taught in govt schools for several decades.Restricting the recruitment, it said, could affect students studying these languages as well as employment opportunities for qualified language teachers.It sought three measures: recruitment of high-school teachers for all recognised languages, creation of separate language-teacher posts based on the number of students studying each language, and introduction of AI as a separate subject rather than as a replacement for the third language.The forum said such measures would help preserve Karnataka’s multilingual education system while enabling students to acquire skills in emerging technologies.You Can articles.title: Jayden Daniels to visit with specialists after sustaining dislocated elbow in loss to Cowboys
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels is once again battling a dislocated elbow.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders find themselves in a familiar — and unfortunate — situation after star quarterback Jayden Daniels left Sunday's game with a dislocated left elbow. After undergoing further testing Monday, Daniels will meet with specialists to consult on the injury, Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Monday.

Quinn added the team won't have a major update on Daniels until those meetings happen. For now, however, the Commanders are not looking to bring in another quarterback.

Daniels sustained the injury on the final play of the first half in a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys . With the Commanders looking to score before halftime, Daniels took a snap from under center, but awkwardly tripped after one of his linemen appeared to step on his foot, knocking him off-balance. As he was going to the ground, Daniels used his left arm to brace himself.

After chucking the ball incomplete, Daniels lay on the turf until he was eventually carted off the field.

It was a gruesome injury, one that caused Tom Brady — who was in the broadcast booth — to utter an expletive live on the air . Brady quickly apologized for swearing.

After the contest, the Commanders head coach revealed Daniels was dealing with a dislocated left elbow. Quinn added that X-rays did not show a fracture, but that Daniels would undergo additional testing Monday.

It's an injury that Daniels has dealt with before. The 25-year-old missed four games last season due to a dislocated left elbow . He returned to action, but reinjured himself in his first game back and was shut down for the rest of the year. Quinn said Monday that surgery was not mentioned last season, with a source telling ESPN that Daniels did not sustain ligament damage last year, which is why surgery was not recommended at the time.

That injury completely derailed what was supposed to be a star-studded second season for the quarterback. As a rookie, Daniels looked like a future superstar. After being selected No. 2 overall from LSU by the Commanders, Daniels threw 25 touchdowns against nine interceptions as a rookie, leading Washington to the playoffs and making the Pro Bowl in his first year.

His numbers took a massive downturn in Year 2 due to various injuries. Daniels started just seven games last season, tossing eight touchdowns against three interceptions.

With those injuries seemingly behind him, Daniels opened the 2026 NFL season looking to get back on track. After a slow start in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles , Daniels rallied late to nearly lead his team to a win.

The quarterback was off to a modest start against the Cowboys before leaving the contest at the end of the first half.

With Daniels once again sidelined, the Commanders will turn to veteran Marcus Mariota in Week 3. The 32-year-old Mariota performed admirably when pressed into action last season, but went just 2-6 in his eight starts.

articles.title: How Dak Prescott built his $295 million wealth: Inside the Cowboys quarterback’s business empire beyond football
articles.summary: NFL News: Dak Prescott has made most of his money from football, but the Dallas Cowboys quarterback has also spent years building a business portfolio away from.
articles.body: Dak Prescott has made most of his money from football, but the Dallas Cowboys quarterback has also spent years building a business portfolio away from the NFL. His earnings from massive contracts have given him a strong financial base, while his investments have taken him into restaurants, fitness technology, beverages, truck accessories and sports education. Together, these moves show how Prescott has looked beyond his career on the football field and started building a business empire of his own.Dak Prescott’s NFL earnings and restaurant, fitness and beverage investmentsPrescott’s NFL career remains the biggest part of his wealth. The Cowboys signed him to a four-year, $160 million contract in 2021, giving him one of the largest deals of his career at that point. In 2024, he agreed to another four-year extension worth $240 million, including $231 million guaranteed and an $80 million signing bonus. OverTheCap lists his career NFL earnings at more than $295 million.But Prescott has not simply relied on his football salary. In 2021, he became a 20% owner of four Walk-On’s Sports Bistreaux locations in Texas. The restaurants are in Arlington, Las Colinas, The Colony and Waco. Walk-On’s is a Louisiana-based sports restaurant chain known for Louisiana-style food, and the investment also had a personal connection for Prescott because he grew up in Bossier City, Louisiana.His investment in the restaurant business was limited to those four locations rather than the entire Walk-On’s chain, giving him a direct ownership interest in the restaurants while adding another business to his growing portfolio.Prescott has also invested in OxeFit, a fitness technology company based in Plano, Texas. The company develops strength and fitness equipment that uses robotics, sensors and artificial intelligence. OxeFit raised $12.5 million in Series A funding in 2021, with Prescott among the investors.Another part of his portfolio is GLOW Beverages, where Prescott became an equity stakeholder and brand ambassador. The company makes functional drinks focused on hydration and energy. Forbes reported in 2023 that Prescott had invested in GLOW alongside other investors, including Kylie Jenner. Forbes also estimated that Prescott earned $12 million off the field in 2022.Dak Prescott expands his business empire with RealTruck, IMG Academy and Tequila VolteoPrescott’s investments have also taken him into businesses that have little connection to the restaurant or fitness industries. One example is RealTruck, an online retailer that sells truck accessories and customization products. In 2022, RealTruck said Prescott and other professional athletes had invested in the company through Patricof Co. Prescott was also named to the company’s strategic advisory team, giving him a role beyond simply putting money into the business.His portfolio later expanded into sports education. Prescott invested in IMG Academy in November 2023, according to Bloomberg reporting cited by Yahoo Sports. IMG Academy is known for its sports training and education programs, making the investment another way for Prescott to stay connected to the sports world while building wealth outside the NFL.Prescott also entered the beverage alcohol business through Tequila Volteo, a Dallas-based tequila startup. D Magazine reported in 2025 that Prescott invested in the company in 2024. A portion of sales also benefits his Faith Fight Finish Foundation.With more than $295 million in documented NFL earnings and investments spread across several industries, Prescott’s financial story goes beyond his Cowboys salary. articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had NFL fans wondering if he had discovered a very different kind of pregame ritual. articles.body: Travis Kelce may still have plenty left to give the Kansas City Chiefs, but his growing business interests suggest he is also thinking about life beyond football. The 36-year-old tight end has taken a major step into baseball ownership, joining the Cleveland Guardians' ownership group. For Kelce, the investment is more than a financial move. It brings him closer to the city that shaped his life and career.Travis Kelce joins Cleveland Guardians ownership groupKelce's latest venture marks a meaningful homecoming for the NFL star. Born and raised in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, the Chiefs tight end has become part of the ownership group of the Cleveland Guardians, a baseball team reportedly valued at $1.7 billion.The investment gives Kelce a new role in professional sports, this time away from the football field. However, he will have to wait until after the 2027 season before he can become a majority owner.For Kelce, the connection runs far deeper than business. Cleveland remains a central part of his identity, and his latest move reflects the lasting bond he shares with his hometown.Speaking about the investment, Kelce said, “I have so much love for this city.“I say it all the time: I’m just a kid from the Heights living the dream.“I credit every good thing in my life to Cleveland and being raised here with the values and the people and the work ethic.“Cleveland Heights is such a diverse and dynamic place. articles.title: ‘He Should Not Be Starting,’ ‘What Are We Doing?’ — Buccaneers Fans React to HC Todd Bowles Contradicting Rueben Bain Jr. Over Injury Status
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gotten off to a surprisingly poor start this season. After losing to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1, they fell to the Clevela...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gotten off to a surprisingly poor start this season. After losing to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1, they fell to the Cleveland Browns in their home opener in a dreadful performance. Now the Buccaneers sit 0-2, and plenty of panic is spreading among the fanbase.

The Buccaneers need to be better on both sides of the ball, but a few specific players have been called out for low production. One is rookie defensive end Rueben Bain Jr. While it usually takes rookies some time to get acclimated to the NFL, the team needs something from their first-round pick given how much they are struggling on defense.

Buccaneers Fans Critical of Rueben Bain Jr.'s Situation

Bain looked dominant during training camp, and that raised the level of expectation for the rookie in his first season. However, we have not seen the same player in the first two weeks. Bain insists he is not injured, but Bucs head coach Todd Bowles is not convinced.

JoeBucsFan.com reported that "Bain says the shoulder is not affecting his play, per Bowles. However, it sounded like Bowles is skeptical."

"I don't think he's completely healthy," Bowles said of Bain. "But at the same time, he's good enough to play. We've got to get more production there."

For Latest Information: NFL Injury Report

Bowles' comments seem to contradict what the rookie believes about his health, and the team's fans were quick to react to it.

Joshua A. Martin said on X, "If Bain is not healthy, sit him down! He deserves to be out on the field healthy. He clearly isn't the same player as we seen during the preseason/training camp."

One fan wrote, "Then he should not be starting," in reference to Bowles saying Bain isn't fully healthy.

Another fan added, "Currently looks like Walker is better at this point if Bain isn't healthy – WTF we doing here?!"

The Walker referenced is David Walker , the Bucs' fourth-round pick last season. In limited snaps, he recorded a sack against the Browns, and that is more than you can say for Bain.

Evan T on X had a similar response to Bain playing many more snaps than Walker. He said, "David Walker played like what — 3 snaps and had a sack? What are we doing???????"

It seems like Buccaneers fans are fed up with the defensive rotations to begin the season. Most of that is directed at Bowles, a defense-minded head coach who has the final say on who is on the field.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Through two games, the Bucs are giving up 28 points per game, and their defense is ranked 15th on PFN's Defense Impact Metric . That won't cut it, especially for a team whose offense has struggled so far.

The Bucs have plenty of time to turn their season around, but they need more on both sides of the ball. Developing Bain and other rookies will also go a long way toward their being successful.

Naresh said on X, "My big worry is he is not gonna get properly developed because of this Coaching Staff."

Bowles may find himself on the hot seat if he does not turn things around fast. Buccaneers fans aren't used to being uncompetitive, and that is the path they are currently on.

articles.summary: There were some pretty vicious Caleb Williams memes, but others were downright funny. Perhaps even to Caleb himself.
articles.body:
The good news for Bears QB Caleb Williams is that his injured hamstring is about as good as he or the team could have hoped.

The bad news? Social media is roasting Williams' real-time reaction to the injury when it happened. Some are funny. Others are downright vicious, questioning the toughness of the same quarterback who got beat to a pulp as a rookie.

If you watched Williams go down late in Sunday's game, it was a pretty shocking moment. He fell untouched and writhed in pain, unable to get up immediately. Solder Field, already a bit down after a bad offensive day and three hours in the rain, fell silent.

Now that we know Williams' hamstring didn't detach from the bone, it was open season. You knew it was bound to happen.

The Keyboard Corps is really leaning into the same through line on most of these: that being carted off for a short-term injury is a serious affront. Even former NFL players got in on the action.

But we're going to veer away from that type of response. Some of the Williams memes were downright funny. These were jokes that maybe even Williams could possibly laugh at. You know, when he's feeling better. (Watch it!)

It felt like this one was made specifically for my wife.

Anyone who has kids knows this one is good.

I'd rather step on a jellyfish than a Lego piece. Seriously. They're colored caltrops for kids.

Lieutenant Dan had more than a grade-1 hammy.

There actually were multiple "Forrest Gump"-related memes, including this well-worn trope.

This is absurd, but mesmerizingly funny, too.

This one has a whole series, including burning your mouth on a Hot Pocket …

This is just good, clean fun from where I'm sitting.

Williams is going to be asked about this — or these memes — at some point. Maybe it's not this week, as head coach Ben Johnson said Williams might not practice. But eventually, Williams will be asked.

I'll be curious about his reaction to them. There are some parallels to the Paul Pierce situation from a generation ago. In Game 1 of the 2008 NBA Finals, Pierce had to be carried off the floor, yet he miraculously returned in just a few game minutes to make a few buckets and go on to win Finals MVP.

The backstory of that one isn't clear. Did Pierce really use the "injury" as an excuse to use the commode? Maybe, even if Pierce's story has wavered on that one over the years.

If Williams has fun with it, it could turn in his favor. If not? It might be the kind of thing fans hang around his neck for every tough game, every tough playoff loss or — yep — every time he gets hurt in a game.

We'd hate to see that. And you can probably tell, these memes are mostly in the we-all-can-laugh-without-being-mean category. Some are downright terrific.

The rest? Most of us have already moved on from those.

articles.title: Before raising two Super Bowl champions, Donna Kelce faced the challenges of motherhood that shaped the Kelce brothers’ rise to greatnes
articles.summary: NFL News: Long before Donna Kelce became one of the most recognisable mothers in the NFL, her days revolved around work, family responsibilities and two energet.
articles.body: Long before Donna Kelce became one of the most recognisable mothers in the NFL, her days revolved around work, family responsibilities and two energetic boys who rarely sat still. Raising Jason and Travis Kelce brought plenty of challenges, and there was no guarantee either son would reach professional football. Behind their remarkable careers was a mother learning, sacrificing and finding her way through the demanding journey of parenthood.Donna Kelce called motherhood the hardest challenge of her lifeFor Donna Kelce, raising two sons was a very different experience from building a career. The former commercial banker worked hard to support her family, but the responsibilities of motherhood brought a level of uncertainty that no job could match.In an October 2024 interview with Glamour, Donna reflected on the demands of raising Jason and Travis, offering a candid look at the challenges behind her family’s success.“Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work,” Donna said.She went on to explain why parenting could feel so overwhelming, especially when children depended on her for almost everything.“But raising children, when they’re totally dependent on you and you’re trying to do the best you can with the limited resources that you have, it’s the most daunting task I’ve ever had to do.”Her words revealed a side of Donna that fans do not always see. Today, she is often celebrated for her sons’ achievements, but her own story includes the everyday pressure of providing for a family while trying to make the right decisions for two growing children.Donna was also a major breadwinner, balancing professional responsibilities with the needs of her family. The experience demanded time, energy and careful choices. Unlike football, where a season eventually ends, motherhood offered no clear finish line.Raising Jason and Travis Kelce meant handling a house full of energyJason and Travis grew up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, where sports became a major part of their lives. But their childhoods were not built around a carefully planned path to the NFL.The brothers tried different sports, including hockey, basketball and lacrosse. Football became a bigger part of their lives later, after they reached seventh grade.Before college recruiters showed interest, Donna was simply raising two active boys. Their energy often kept the household on its toes, and she has recalled the broken windows and calls from neighbours that came with their childhood antics.Still, Donna made a point of explaining that her sons were not bad children. They were lively, competitive and often difficult to keep occupied.In a 2024 interview with Us Weekly, she recalled how important it was to keep the boys busy.“Jason and Travis were very active, and if we wanted any sanity in the household at all, we knew we had to keep them extremely busy,” Donna said.The family also had to consider the cost of keeping up with two children involved in activities. Donna and her former husband, Ed Kelce, had to weigh the financial demands of raising their sons while making sure they had opportunities to explore their interests.Those years may not have looked extraordinary at the time. Yet they helped establish the routine, discipline and family support that became important as Jason and Travis pursued football more seriously.Donna Kelce put respect and kindness ahead of football fameDonna never needed her sons to become NFL stars to feel proud of them. Her focus as a mother was on the people they would become, not just the careers they might build.She has spoken about teaching Jason and Travis to treat everyone with respect, regardless of their position or status. In a 2024 interview with Us Weekly, Donna explained the lesson she wanted her sons to carry into adulthood.“I just wanted to make sure that they treated everyone the same. I said, ‘I don’t care if they’re the individuals who are cleaning the toilets or they’re the CEO of organizations,’” Donna said. “It’s basically, treat everybody with respect, like you would want to be treated.”That principle offered a foundation beyond the football field. Professional sports can bring fame, money and public attention, but Donna wanted her sons to remember that character matters regardless of success.Her approach also meant allowing Jason and Travis to develop their own identities. Their paths were not identical. Jason became a standout centre for the Philadelphia Eagles, while Travis built his career as a tight end for the Kansas City Chiefs.Both reached the highest level of the sport, but their success came through different experiences, decisions and challenges. Donna’s role was not to script their futures. It was to support them as they found their way.The Kelce brothers’ Super Bowl moment made Donna’s sacrifices unforgettableDonna’s years of parenting took on a new meaning when Jason and Travis faced each other in Super Bowl LVII in February 2023. Jason’s Eagles met Travis’ Chiefs, creating the first Super Bowl matchup between two brothers.For Donna, the game presented an emotional dilemma no parent would easily resolve. One son would celebrate a championship, while the other would walk away disappointed.Rather than choosing a side, she wore a split jersey representing both teams. The image quickly became one of the defining moments of that Super Bowl, capturing the pride and conflict of a mother whose sons had reached the same extraordinary stage.The game also brought renewed attention to the family’s journey. Jason and Travis had gone from two energetic boys growing up in Ohio to Super Bowl champions, each with a career that millions of fans followed.Yet Donna’s own reflections make clear that the journey was never just about trophies. She had spent years balancing work, family finances and the unpredictable demands of raising children. She had watched her sons grow, make mistakes, discover their strengths and pursue their ambitions.Jason and Travis’ achievements are theirs, earned through years of effort and commitment. But Donna’s influence remains part of their story, from the values she taught them to the support she offered long before the cameras arrived.For Donna Kelce, the most meaningful reward may not be the Super Bowl rings or the recognition that followed. It is seeing the boys she raised become successful adults, loving fathers and men who still value the family that helped shape them.Sources: Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year interview · Us Weekly’s profile of Donna Kelce · TIME’s interview with Donna Kelce .Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mike Evans Injury Update, Latest on 49ers WR, Fantasy Outlook and Top Waiver-Wire Targets
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Monday that Mike Evans' injured hip will "have to be managed this week" after the veteran wideout left Sunday's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins with the issue and didn't return.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Monday that Mike Evans' injured hip will "have to be managed this week" after the veteran wideout left Sunday's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins with the issue and didn't return.

Shanahan did suggest on Sunday that Evans' injury wasn't serious.

"It can always change tomorrow," he told reporters after the game. "But if the game was different, he would've been able to come back in."

That was an important update for a Niners team already without De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson at the receiver position, leaving Evans and Deebo Samuel as the top options out wide for Brock Purdy.

It would be good news for fantasy football enthusiasts relying on Evans this season, though if he's forced to miss time, there are options on the waiver wire.

In Las Vegas, Tre Tucker is coming off a fantastic game (five catches for 119 yards and a touchdown), though the potential return of Brock Bowers could limit his targets. Still, he's clearly emerged as Kirk Cousins' preferred target among the team's wideouts.

Monitor Zay Flowers' status in Baltimore. If he misses Week 3, Rashod Bateman—who caught seven passes for 88 yards and a score with Flowers out of the lineup on Sunday—is a good short-term add.

In Philadelphia, Dontayvion Wicks continues to impress as the No. 2 wideout behind DeVonta Smith, putting up seven catches for 147 yards and a score after two games. Expect Jalen Hurts to continue relying on him in the passing game with Dallas Goedert scheduled to be out of action for a few weeks with a strained MCL.

Finally, it appears Denzel Boston has emerged as a trusted target for Deshaun Watson in Cleveland. The rookie second-rounder has seven catches for 154 yards and two touchdowns on the season and is tied with KC Concepcion for the team-lead in targets (11).

Trusting anybody on the Browns never feels great, but Boston is off to a very promising start and is worth your consideration.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy 'committed' to offense built around Aaron Rodgers, points to offensive line play as source of unit's struggles
articles.summary: As long as Pittsburgh's offense remains toothless, McCarthy will continue to field questions about his starting quarterback. At some point, pointing to the o...
articles.body:
Through two games, the Pittsburgh Steelers have one of the worst offenses in the NFL, ranking 30th out of 32 teams with 249.5 yards per game and 30th with 23 total points.

Pittsburgh's defense accounts for seven of those points thanks to a pick 6 by T.J. Watt in Week 1's 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons .

Pittsburgh's offensive woes took center stage Sunday in a listless 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots . The Steelers managed just 235 yards on 3.5 yards per play. They advanced to the red zone once in the game's final minutes and turned the ball over when they got there.

Aaron Rodgers threw one interception and fumbled twice; one was recovered by the Patriots for a scoop-and-score touchdown that iced New England 's win.

Rodgers was under pressure throughout the game and frequently resorted to check downs and short passes when he was able to get rid of the ball while averaging 4.8 yards per attempt. He was sacked four times and hit seven others.

Pittsburgh's running backs were repeatedly met by Patriots defenders at or near the line of scrimmage.

McCarthy 'committed' to plan around Rodgers

On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy was asked frequently about Pittsburgh's offensive struggles during his weekly news conference . Two topics came up repeatedly: Pittsburgh's offensive line and Rodgers.

McCarthy remained steadfast in his support of Rodgers and the value he believes the 42-year-old former four-time MVP brings to the team.

"We have a quarterback that has an incredible wealth of experience," McCarthy said. "And we've built this offense based on his experiences and to play to his strengths. He's knows that, and I'm committed to it."

McCarthy instead pointed to Pittsburgh's offensive line as the primary source of the Steelers' offensive struggles.

"We're a protection-first unit, and that wasn't the case yesterday," McCarthy said. "Our quarterback was hit too much yesterday."

McCarthy took some of the blame of the unit's struggles due to his preseason strategy of rotating players in and out of spots on the offensive line. He believes that the line will improve with more reps together as the season progresses.

"I think in hindsight you go back and you look: how many days did we line up with the same offensive line?" McCarthy said. "We worked a lot of different combinations. No excuses, but they need continuity.

"They need reps, they need consistency. So the consistency will come through the common concepts."

In an ideal football world, an NFL unit isn't going into Week 3 of the regular season without enough reps to have cohesion. Pittsburgh's offensive line struggles are real and playing a significant impact on the unit's slow start.

Will McCarthy hold Rodgers accountable for poor play?

But that doesn't address the questions around Rodgers. At 42 years old with an Achilles tendon that's been repaired, Rodgers isn't remotely close to the form that led him to four MVPs and a Super Bowl title with the Green Bay Packers . He hasn't been for years.

Rodgers won that Super Bowl with McCarthy as his head coach, and the two have a relationship built on those objectively better times. For now, McCarthy remains firmly in Rodgers' corner in his first year as Pittsburgh's head coach.

But as long as Pittsburgh's offense remains toothless, McCarthy will continue to field questions about his starting quarterback. At some point, if this continues, pointing to the offensive line won't be a satisfactory answer.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's retirement dilemma takes a dramatic turn after Andy Reid's bold challenge
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is giving the Kansas City Chiefs plenty of reasons to keep believing in him. At 36, the veteran tight end is still making game-changing p.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is giving the Kansas City Chiefs plenty of reasons to keep believing in him. At 36, the veteran tight end is still making game-changing plays, adding to his remarkable NFL résumé and showing no signs of slowing down. His latest milestone has now drawn a playful response from Andy Reid, who appears more than happy to give Kelce another reason to stay in Kansas City. With retirement talk still lingering, the Chiefs coach has a challenge that could keep his star tight end chasing history.Andy Reid sends Travis Kelce a record-breaking challengeKelce's latest performance against the Indianapolis Colts offered another reminder of his value to Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. Kansas City survived a thrilling 33-30 overtime battle, with the tight end recording nine catches for 101 yards and a touchdown.However, one moment stood out beyond the final score. Kelce surpassed Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk to become the NFL's all-time leader in receiving yards after the catch. He finished the game with 6,288 career yards after the catch, adding another major achievement to his growing legacy.Reid's reaction captured the spirit of Kelce's ongoing pursuit of greatness.“I see Kelce broke another record. He hangs around long enough, he’ll break all of ‘em,” Matt Foster shared Coach Reid’s response on X.The remark carried a playful tone, but it also highlighted how much Kelce still has to offer. Reid has watched the tight end develop into one of the league's most productive players, and his latest comments suggest there is no rush to see that partnership end.Travis Kelce's NFL records add another twist to retirement talkKelce's achievements are becoming harder to ignore as retirement speculation follows him into the 2026 season. He entered the campaign needing to prove he could still perform at a high level, and his first two games have offered encouraging signs.Before the Colts game, Kelce had already moved past Jason Witten for second place on the all-time receiving yards list among tight ends. He now has 13,174 regular-season receiving yards, 1,092 catches and 83 touchdowns.His postseason numbers are just as impressive. Kelce owns the NFL record for playoff receptions with 178 and entered the season 168 receiving yards shy of Jerry Rice's postseason yardage record of 2,245.Yet Kelce has made it clear that personal motivation, rather than chasing numbers alone, will shape his future.“I still think I can go out and play at a high level, and I want to go out there and prove to myself that I can play at a better level than I did last year,” Kelce said.“I think that’s probably the biggest thing for me is making sure that I’m accountable for the guys in this room every single play that I’m out there.”For now, Kelce's production gives Kansas City every reason to enjoy the present. articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart has reportedly suffered a sprained MCL, with Ian Rapoport of NFL Network providing additional details:
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart has reportedly suffered a sprained MCL, with Ian Rapoport of NFL Network providing additional details:

Head coach John Harbaugh discussed the injury after the game:

Dart exited Monday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams in the first quarter after taking a big hit in the pocket. He suffered a left knee injury and was taken to the locker room after staying down on the field for some time before walking off under his own power.

Dart was eventually ruled out of the game with a knee injury, although general manager Joe Schoen had a positive outlook:

Despite the injury, he reportedly wanted to go back into the game:

As a rookie in 2025, Dart provided excitement and hope for a struggling franchise. He took over the reins of the offense in Week 4 and completed 63.7 percent of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions in 12 starts. He also rushed for 487 yards and nine touchdowns.

The No. 25 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft has unfortunately taken some big hits, though, and one of them led to a concussion against the Chicago Bears last Nov. 16 that cost him the next two games.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan provided the details: "Dart took a hard hit on a fumble in the third quarter, getting hit from the side as he ran by a defensive lineman tracking back to make the play. His head hit the ground, and he got up slowly, eventually walking to the sideline after remaining on the field for a few seconds on his knees. Dart returned to the game the following drive for two plays and then went to the blue medical tent in between quarters. He walked slowly into the locker room afterward with a trainer. The first-round pick was ruled out later in the fourth quarter."

Dart is the present and future in New York as the Giants look to break a malaise that's seen the team post losing records 11 times in 13 seasons.

New York does have a solid backup quarterback though in Jameis Winston, who led the offense to success last season against the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions while Dart was out.

Over those two starts, Winston threw for 567 yards and two touchdowns (two interceptions) while adding a rushing touchdown as well as a receiving score on a trick play in the Detroit game.

articles.title: Why did Julian Edelman defend Tom Brady? The Former Patriots star reacts to the NFL legend’s NSFW Cowboys vs. Commanders commentary

articles.body: Tom Brady gave NFL fans an unfiltered look at his FOX Sports booth personality during the Dallas Cowboys’ 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders on September 20, 2026. His NSFW comments quickly caught attention.However, his former New England Patriots teammate Julian Edelman saw the lighter side. One day later, Edelman explained why Brady’s loose commentary did not bother him and instead made the seven-time Super Bowl champion sound more natural on television. Julian Edelman loved seeing a more unfiltered Tom BradyDuring the recent episode of “The Gronk & Jules Show”, Edelman backed Brady after the broadcaster swore while reacting to Jayden Daniels’ elbow injury.“I think he’s showing that he’s human,” Edelman said on the show. “My favorite by far was the piss missile. That was a cherry on top.”The first slip came during the second quarter. FOX showed a replay after Daniels suffered an elbow injury following an awkward fall. Brady reacted instantly with, “Oh s—!” He then caught himself and added, “Excuse me. Was not expecting to see that.”Later, Brady found another memorable phrase while breaking down Dak Prescott’s deep completion to CeeDee Lamb. Prescott hit Lamb down the right sideline in the fourth quarter, and Brady called the throw an “absolute piss missile.”He said, “Absolute piss missile up the sideline. [Mike Sainristil] is still sticking in Cover 2, and CeeDee settles in that hole. [Quan Martin] can’t get over there on time. Little bit of a high-risk throw, but when you got arm strength like that, and you make a decisive read with a clean pocket, one little hitch into that, you can really drive it, and there was no margin of error on that throw.”The former quarterback then explained the play rather than simply praising Prescott’s arm. He pointed out that Washington stayed in Cover 2 while Lamb settled into the open area, leaving Prescott with very little room for error.Edelman clearly enjoyed that moment. He even called the phrase the “cherry on top” of Brady’s broadcast.Rob Gronkowski also backed Tom Brady after his live TV slip-upsEdelman was not alone in defending Brady. Rob Gronkowski, another former Patriots teammate, joined the conversation during the same episode, and praised Brady’s comfort in the booth.The reaction comes as Brady continues his third season as FOX Sports’ lead NFL analyst. He joined the network after retiring from the NFL in 2023, working alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt.Brady also took a shot at Washington wide receiver Stefon Diggs during the September 20 broadcast. After Diggs celebrated a Week 1 touchdown against Philadelphia by grabbing the goalpost, the NFL fined him $14,926. When Diggs appeared to imitate the celebration against Dallas, Brady joked, “No more humping the goalpost for Diggs.”In Edelman’s case, though, the biggest takeaway came from Brady simply sounding like himself. articles.title: Darius Slayton, Colts Reportedly Agree to Contract Amid Alec Pierce Injury, Latest Fantasy Impact
articles.summary: After being released by the New York Giants before the start of the season, Darius Slayton is back on an NFL roster.
articles.body:
After being released by the New York Giants before the start of the season, Darius Slayton is back on an NFL roster.

Per NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Indianapolis Colts signed the veteran receiver on Monday after Alec Pierce suffered a heel injury against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday.

Slayton spent the first seven years of his career with the Giants, racking up 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns. In 2025, he had 538 yards and a touchdown in 14 games.

With New York adding Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr. this offseason, the release of Slayton wasn't all that surprising. The Giants also saved over $3 million in cap space by releasing him.

Now, he'll get the chance to reunite with Daniel Jones in Indianapolis. Slayton's best seasons came when he was catching passes from Jones, and he'll look to get back to his best form with the Colts.

As for how big a role he'll play in Indianapolis, that depends on how long Piece is out. According to Joel A. Erickson of the Indianapolis Star, Pierce is "likely" going to be out for several weeks, so the Colts will need some players to step up in the meantime.

Josh Downs will presumably be Jones' first option, and he played well after Pierce's exit on Sunday, catching seven passes for 72 yards in the overtime loss to the Chiefs.

Keenan Allen will likely get more targets as well, and Indianapolis will need to rely on tight end Tyler Warren more in the coming weeks. Slayton will certainly have the chance to play a big role, but he might not be worth fantasy managers picking up just yet.

He'll look to settle in with the Colts over the next week before potentially making his debut against the Houston Texans on Sunday.

articles.title: Is Aaron Rodgers already regretting his NFL comeback? Former Patriots legend raises concerns after the Pittsburgh Steelers’ heartbreaking start to the season
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers came back to the NFL for one final season with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Two games into that farewell campaign, though, the offense has s.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers came back to the NFL for one final season with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Two games into that farewell campaign, though, the offense has struggled badly. After Sunday’s 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots on September 20, questions about Rodgers’ decision to return have already started.For Rodgers, the plan looked far more promising a week earlier. The Steelers beat the Atlanta Falcons 20-13 in Mike McCarthy’s first game as head coach. Rodgers threw for 221 yards and a touchdown. Since then, the picture has changed quickly. Rob Gronkowski thinks Aaron Rodgers could already be second-guessing his returnFormer Patriots star Rob Gronkowski took the question a step further after the Steelers’ loss. During the recent episode of “The Gronk & Jules Show,” Gronkowski suggested Rodgers may already wish he had retired after the 2025 season.“Aaron Rodgers is probably thinking that he should have retired last year,” Gronkowski said during the show while discussing Pittsburgh’s first two games.Julian Edelman pushed back on the idea, pointing out that the season had only reached Week 2. Gronkowski still stood by his point, saying the Steelers had shown little life on offense.“There’s just no juice on that offensive side of the ball,” Gronkowski said on the same episode.That criticism became harder to ignore after Pittsburgh’s trip to New England. The Steelers struggled to sustain drives and failed to score a touchdown. Their only points came from a Chris Boswell field goal, while the Patriots’ defense kept Rodgers under pressure for much of the afternoon.The Steelers also finished the game with just 235 total yards. Pittsburgh converted only 3 of 13 third-down attempts, giving the offense little chance to stay on the field. Those numbers help explain why Gronkowski focused so heavily on the lack of production. Aaron Rodgers now faces pressure to change the conversationRodgers struggled against New England on September 20. He completed 23 of 39 passes for 187 yards and threw one interception. He also lost a fumble that New England returned for a touchdown. The Patriots held Pittsburgh to 235 total yards in the 20-3 win.That leaves Rodgers and the Steelers at 1-1 after two weeks. The defense has produced big plays, but the offense has yet to find a steady rhythm.The situation also adds weight to Rodgers’ decision to return. He entered 2026 knowing this would be his final NFL season, and the Steelers reunited him with McCarthy, his former Green Bay coach.Rodgers has also dealt with plenty of attention around his return because he spent much of the 2025 offseason considering his future before ultimately choosing to continue his career. Now, the quarterback has to turn that decision into results on the field. A stronger offensive showing would quickly quiet the retirement talk, while another flat performance could make Gronkowski’s question even louder.Gronkowski’s retirement question may be an early overreaction, as Edelman noted. Still, after two games, Rodgers has given critics plenty to discuss.
