1. Jamari Johnson , Oregon (8.4) 2. Trey'Dez Green , LSU (8.0)

Green suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter of Saturday's game against the Ole Miss Rebels. While the injury may not be serious now, it could be a long-term issue.

At 6'7", the tight end will get hit regularly around the knees and midsection. His calling card as a prospect centers on being an explosive/physical runner after the catch. His talent and improvement so far this season are apparent, as long as he can take the pounding and keep bouncing back.

Best Run-Blocker : Trevor Lauck Best Pass-Blocker : Jordan Seaton Best Zone-Blocker : Trevor Lauck Most Pro-Ready : Trevor Goosby Most Versatile : Trevor Lauck

1. Jordan Seaton , LSU (8.1) 2. Trevor Goosby , Texas (7.9) 3. Trevor Lauck , Iowa (7.8)

Seaton is the 2027 class' most physically talented tackle due to his size (6'5", 311 lbs), length and movement skills in pass protection. He's a rare prospect comfortable working in one-on-one situations. Conversely, Seaton isn't the most polished run blocker in terms of sustaining control throughout reps. Although, his footwork, raw power and flashes of finishing with authority indicate an untapped ceiling.

Best Run-Blocker : Anthonie Knapp Best Pass-Blocker : Greg Johnson Best Zone-Blocker : Kade Pieper Most Pro-Ready : Anthonie Knapp Most Versatile : Samson Okunlola

1. Anthonie Knapp , Notre Dame (7.9) 2. Kade Pieper , Iowa (7.7) 3. Samson Okunlola , Miami (7.7) 4. Greg Johnson , Minnesota (7.5)

Explain the Grade : Anthonie Knapp, Notre Dame

Knapp moved from left tackle to left guard this season and immediately made an impact. The opportunity to operate in a more controlled environment flanked by two blockers allows his high-end play-strength to shine. Knapp is stout at the point of attack, with the body control to stay attached and finish reps. When his grip-strength is factored into the equation, the tackle convert has the ability to end reps once clamped. So far this season, the junior prospect has looked like a natural fit working along the interior.

Best Speed-Rusher : Dylan Stewart Best Power-Rusher : Yhonzae Pierre Best Run-Stopper : Kenyatta Jackson Most Versatile : Matayo Uiagalelei

1. Colin Simmons , Texas (8.5) 2. Dylan Stewart , South Carolina (8.4) 3. Yhonzae Pierre , Alabama (8.0) 4. Will Heldt , Clemson (8.0) 5. Kenyatta Jackson , Ohio State (7.9) 6. Boubacar Traore , Notre Dame (7.8) 7. Matayo Uiagalelei , Oregon (7.6)

Explain the Grade : Dylan Stewart, South Carolina

Colin Simmons ranked as the class' top edge defender (for now) but not listed among the superlatives may come as a surprise. Of the two, Stewart is the better speed-rusher. However, the gap between the South Carolina defender and his Texas counterpart isn't all that wide. Meanwhile, the latter has a better motor and is more polished to get the nod as the higher-ranked prospect. Also, the South Carolina prospect battled injuries last year and didn't play until Week 3 of this season. Stewart can certainly take over the top edge spot if he hits the ground running from this point forward.

Best Nose Tackle : A'Mauri Washington Best Pass-Rusher : Ahmad Moten Sr. Best Run-Stopper : Will Echoles Most Versatile : David Stone

1. Will Echoles , Ole Miss (8.3) 2. David Stone , Oklahoma (8.1) 3. A'Mauri Washington , Oregon (7.7) 4. Ahmad Moten Jr ., Miami (7.6)

Explain the Grade : David Stone, Oklahoma

The Bleacher Report Scouting Department is still waiting for Stone to really announce himself as a sure-fire first-round pick after relatively slow start in Oklahoma's first two games. However, his traits are tantalizing.

The 6'3", 312-pound defensive tackle has plenty of size and strength to be a disruptive run-defender at the next level. He also moves well, presenting upside as a pass-rusher. At this point, Stone is a gamble. Though his skill set is worth betting on.

Best Blitzer : Whit Weeks Best Run-Stopper : Sammy Brown Best in Coverage : Chris Cole Most Versatile : Whit Weeks

1. Chris Cole , Georgia (7.8) 2. Whit Weeks , LSU (7.7) 3. Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asu , Notre Dame (7.6)

Weeks always jumps off the screen when watching LSU's defense, because he's all over the field. The senior defender displays good instincts against the run, the athleticism to be effective in coverage and added value as a blitzer. He's a flat-out playmaker, which is why the linebacker currently wears the venerated No. 7 for the Tigers.

Weeks was trending toward being a notable prospect in a strong positional class last year until an injury caused a return to school. With less competition among the current cycle's crop of second-level defenders, the 2024 First-Team All-SEC performer could realistically emerge as the class' top 'backer by April.

Best in Man Coverage : Leonard Moore Best in Zone Coverage : Ellis Robinson IV Best Slot Corner : JeRico Washington Most Versatile : Leonard Moore

1. Leonard Moore , Notre Dame (9.5) 2. Ashton Hampton , Clemson (8.2) 3. Zabien Brown , Alabama (7.9) 4. Ellis Robinson IV , Georgia (7.9) 5. Jyaire Hill , Michigan (7.7) 6. Kelley Jones , Mississippi State (7.5)

Explain the Grade : Kelley Jones, Mississippi State

At a listed 6'4" and 205 pounds, with long arms and great athletic ability, Jones is one of the draft class's most imposing figures. He's often mentioned as a first-round possibility, but questions remain about his profile. Bigger corners tend to have transitional concerns when they need to decelerate and change direction. Jones is no different. His man-coverage technique/ability to mirror receivers in space is inconsistent.

However, Jones is an excellent zone defender with great route identification. The junior prospect is also an extremely tough defender when working in the red zone. In the right zone-based system, Jones can thrive. But he should be considered a system fit.

Best in Man Coverage : Peyton Bowen Best in Zone Coverage : KJ Bolden Best Run-Stopper : Bray Hubbard Most Versatile : Brauntae Johnson

1. Brauntae Johnson , Notre Dame (7.9) 2. KJ Bolden , Georgia (7.7) 3. Peyton Bowen , Oklahoma (7.7)

With Brauntae Johnson currently injured, Bolden enters the conversation as college football's best safety. The Bulldog is an explosive defender who punishes ball-carriers. Bolden's athleticism is obvious, but Georgia's early cupcake schedule makes it hard to truly assess his coverage acumen. Can he play on top of the defense? Will he maintain eye discipline better this season? Have his man-coverage skills improved?

Technical questions always surround Georgia defenders. Until Bolden's play answers them, his grade will stay lower than it could be.

articles.title: Jonah Coleman and the Best Week 3 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: We are two weeks into the 2026 NFL season and it's starting to become clear how the coinciding fantasy football campaign will shake out.
articles.body:
We are two weeks into the 2026 NFL season and it's starting to become clear how the coinciding fantasy football campaign will shake out.

Week 2's results allowed managers to sniff out whether some of the Week 1 breakout performances legitimate or simply unsustainable, flash-in-the-pain production. With Week 3 on the horizon, managers can capitalize on emerging trends by playing the waiver wire and turning over the bottom of their rosters.

Injuries to several prominent players have opened the door for previously overlooked backups to step into starring roles, while a handful of young players are leveraging strong early performances to establish themselves as legitimate fantasy weapons.

With that in mind, here are some of the best waiver-wire pickups you can make for Week 3.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 dollar starting budget.

Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers (32 Percent Rostered)

After another impressive performance in Week 2, Young is establishing himself as a must-start fantasy quarterback. The Carolina signal-caller alleviated concerns that his Week 1 performance was a fluke by putting up 24.1 fantasy points in a statement 34-3 win over the rival Atlanta Falcons.

Young's outing came on the heels of an explosive 32.4-point showing. His combined 56.5 fantasy points over the first two weeks have him ranking as a top-five performer at the QB position.

While it's far from guaranteed that Young will continue putting up stellar numbers consistently over the course of the long season, his production has become impossible to ignore. He has another plus matchup on tap in Week 3, facing a Cleveland Browns defense that has allowed 19.1 points per game to opposing passers in 2026.

If your quarterback went down with injury or hasn't delivered the expected results to open the year, don't shy away from picking up Young and plugging him in as your starter.

Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints (48 Percent Rostered)

Shough is proving to be the real deal in the Big Easy. He parlayed a strong finish to the 2025 campaign into a hot start for 2026 and now ranks inside the top-eight for point scorers at the quarterback position through two weeks of play.

Although his production tailed off slightly after a 25.2-point outburst in the opener, Shough still tallied 22.4 points on a cool 27-of-34 passing for 252 yards and a touchdown. He also added 23 yards and a score on nine totes, using his dual-threat talents to lead the Saints to a 24-17 win over the Baltimore Ravens.

Given his consistency as a passer, ability to pick up points on the ground and upside in head coach Kellen Moore's system, Shough is worth rostering in nearly every fantasy format. Barring a collapse, he's a shoo-in to finish as a top-12 QB in 2026.

Michael Penix Jr., Atlanta Falcons (4 Percent Rostered)

The Falcons' abysmal start to the season hit a new low during the team's blowout defeat to the rival Panthers. Given the team's struggles with Cooper Rush under center, it won't be long before Penix is thrust back into the starting lineup.

Although he's still recovering from a major knee injury suffered late last season, Penix is trending towards a return for Week 3. He's far-and-away Atlanta's best hope to turn the season around and will get ample opportunity to jump-start the NFL's worst passing attack.

While he's a risky start in his first game back, Penix is worth stashing in deeper formats and could provide a much-needed jolt at the QB position for desperate managers.

Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos (26 Percent Rostered)

Coleman's status as a preseason sleeper looked to be in jeopardy after he failed to log a single offensive touch in his NFL debut. Things changed drastically in Week 2, however, as the fourth-round rookie picked up 58 yards and a touchdown on the first 13 touches of his career.

With fellow Broncos rushers RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins now both dealing with hamstring injuries, Coleman and special teamer Tyler Badie are the only healthy backs left on Denver's roster. While Badie did get a trio of touches in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, Coleman is the clear leader of the platoon with Harvey and Dobbins sidelined.

Even if Dobbins and/or Harvey can give it a go when the Broncos take on the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3, Coleman seems to have done enough to carve out a key role in the team's backfield rotation. He should only gain more playing time and touches as the season wears on.

Any manager who needs RB help or is simply looking to bolster their depth should make Coleman their top waiver-wire target ahead of Week 3. He can be started as a borderline RB2 if both Dobbins and Harvey are out and still retains flex appeal if one or both of his platoonmates are available.

Tank Bigsby, Philadelphia Eagles (29 Percent Rostered)

Philadelphia's shrewd acquisition of Bigsby early last season may pay off in a big way if starting running back Saquon Barkley misses some time. The feature back suffered a stinger early in Week 2, and while he returned to action in the second half, isn't guaranteed to be ready for the team's upcoming clash with the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football .

Will Shipley saw the slight majority of snaps during Barkley's first-half absence, but Bigsby was far and away the more productive player and earned nearly double the volume of his fellow backup. Bigsby finished the game with 11.8 fantasy points after putting up 37 yards and a touchdown on 15 touches, while Shipley only mustered 4.9 points stemming from his 29 yards on nine touches.

Bigsby has consistently faired well whenever he's been green lit for expanded opportunities by the Eagles. Last year, he exploded for 104 yards on nine carries in Week 8 and posted a top-10 weekly finish in his lone start—a Week 18 showing in which he amassed 106 yards and a score on 17 touches.

While Bigsby won't be worth inserting into a lineup outside deeper formats if Barkley is suiting up, he's a great speculative add and can be comfortably deployed if Barkley is out versus the Rams.

Emmanuel Wilson, Seattle Seahawks (1 Percent Rostered)

Despite accumulating more critical injuries in Week 2, Seattle's offense still managed to dominate in a 31-7 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. The ground attack, which saw five different Seahawks log at least one carry and cumulatively put up 162 yards and a touchdown on 40 totes, thrived even after the loss of running back Jadarian Price.

With Price exiting with a shoulder injury, Wilson became the focal point of Seattle's relentless rushing attack. He finished the game with a respectable 92 yards on 21 carries and showed that he can be an impact player when called upon after totaling just three yards on two carries in Week 1.

Don't invest too heavily in acquiring Wilson, as Price doesn't seem to have suffered a serious injury and should return to the field in short order. George Holani remains the preferred third-down back in head coach Klint Kubiak's system and the return of Zach Charbonnet figures to remove any fantasy value Wilson still has left at that point.

Still, Wilson has some value as the clearcut handcuff to Price and can be fired up as a decent fill-in starter in any game the prized rookie misses until Charbonnet comes off the IR.

Denzel Boston, Cleveland Browns (31 Percent Rostered)

In the span of just two weeks, Boston has gone from an overlooked first-year wideout in an underwhelming offense to a player who should be rostered in nearly every fantasy league.

Boston, Cleveland's pick at No. 39 overall in the 2026 draft, opened his career on an intriguing note by catching two of his four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown. He remained off the fantasy radar due to the low volume and his score coming during garbage time in a blowout loss, but his latest performance was too impressive to ignore.

The rookie helped Cleveland pick up a 23-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers by posting a 5/95/1 line on seven targets. That uptick in volume and the production coming during meaningful minutes makes Boston a valid waiver target going into Week 3.

With Boston emerging as the top wideout in Cleveland's offense—he leads the team in targets over the first two games—and facing a distinct lack of competition for looks, fantasy managers should make a run at the rookie before he blows up against a vulnerable Carolina Panthers secondary in Week 3.

Adonai Mitchell, New York Jets (16 Percent Rostered)

Mitchell has oozed potential throughout his two-plus seasons in the NFL, but the 2024 second-round draft pick is finally beginning to reach that lofty ceiling.

After joining the Jets at last year's trade deadline, the benefits of having a full offseason to learn the offense and build chemistry with his teammates has been on display. Mitchell has found his footing as the team's No. 2 wideout, picking up 123 yards on six catches over the first two weeks of the campaign.

While Mitchell's performance in the opener was efficient (3/60/0 on three targets), he benefitted from a heavy amount of volume in Week 2. The receiver reeled in six of his team-high 12 targets for 63 yards to tally 12.3 fantasy points and his first top-30 finish of the campaign.

Garrett Wilson remains Gang Green's unquestioned No. 1 target, but this offense should be able to support two fantasy-relevant receivers in 2026. Mitchell has plug-and-play potential for Week 3 when his side takes on a suspect Detroit Lions defense.

Khalil Shakir, Buffalo Bills (47 Percent Rostered)

The Buffalo Bills' offense is off to a hot start under head coach Joe Brady, with a stellar passing attack leading the way to two consecutive victories. MVP candidate Josh Allen has been spraying the ball around—seven players have logged at least three targets on the year—but Shakir is once again looking like his preferred target when its time to pick up tough yardage and move the chains.

Shakir has only recorded a modest seven catches and 88 receiving yards over the first first two weeks, but 12 targets in that span—second on the team behind tight end Dalton Kincaid—suggest better days are coming.

Even if Shakir isn't putting up matchup-winning numbers, his possession role in Buffalo's offense gives him one of the safest floors of any receiver. He's the perfect player to keep on your bench and deploy as a flex option when bye weeks and injuries sideline your usual starters.

With key offseason pickup DJ Moore suffering a shoulder injury this past week, Shakir could see an uptick in targets starting on Sunday when the team hosts the Los Angeles Chargers.

Tre Tucker, Las Vegas Raiders (29 Percent Rostered)

The Raiders' 2-0 start has been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 season. Tucker was a driving force behind the team's most recent victory, putting up a fantastic 5/119/1 receiving line in a 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Tucker's performance represented a major improvement over his quiet (2/27/0) showing in the opener. His 22.9 fantasy points were good for a top-10 weekly finish, only the third of his NFL career. While Tucker hasn't been much of a fantasy asset in recent seasons, his role as Vegas' No. 1 wideout and the promising play of quarterback Kirk Cousins makes him an interesting pickup.

He'll be a risky start in Week 3 against the New Orleans Saints, but a second consecutive big outing will make Tucker a hot waiver commodity. Get ahead of the potential rush and stash the wideout now if you can afford the roster spot.

Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers (2 Percent Rostered)

It's another tough week for tight end-needy fantasy managers, but Waller could be an answer for those who don't mind rolling the dice on one of the most boom-or-bust players at the position.

Despite logging just three targets in Carolina's 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons, Waller put up 18.3 fantasy points and posted a top-10 finish. The 34-year-old tallied a hyper-efficient 33 yards and a pair of touchdowns on his three catches.

While there is obviously plenty of scoring-based upside with Waller, there's also a good chance he tanks your chances of winning. Waller isn't a big part of the Panthers gameplan—he's played less than half of the offensive snaps —and isn't going to move the needle if he doesn't reach the end zone, evidenced by his 4.8-point showing in a two-catch, 28-yard Week 1 performance.

If you can't find a more stable option via trade, Waller can work as a high-risk, high-reward streaming target for Week 3.

Oronde Gadsden II, Los Angeles Chargers (6 Percent Rostered)

Gadsden's Week 2 numbers may not jump off the page, but a series of injuries have led the second-year tight end to reappear on the fantasy radar for the first time since his breakout rookie season.

While Gadsden only logged two catches and two targets for the second consecutive week, his offensive snap count shot up significantly after both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar were injured during a 26-14 defeat to the Las Vegas Raiders. Gadsden's first touchdown of the year helped him secure a top-15 finish and more TE1-tier numbers could be on the horizon if he remains L.A.'s lone healthy option at the position.

Njoku looks like he'll be out a stretch after being carted off with a knee injury, while Kolar was spotted with his arm in a sling . Gadsden is poised play large number of snaps when the Bolts face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, making him a decent dart throw for managers needing immediate assistance at TE.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (13 Percent Rostered)

Freiermuth came back down to earth this week after opening the year as the TE6, but there's still enough value here to warrant a waiver-wire claim for Week 3.

Aaron Rodgers clearly trusts his veteran tight end, sending five targets his way in each of the first two games. While Freiermuth only converted those looks into four catches and 32 receiving yards during an underwhelming showing against the New England Patriots, he displayed his upside in Week 1 with a 5/46/1 line. He'll have a chance to not only match those marks, but also vastly surpass them when he squares off with the Cincinnati Bengals this week.

The Bengals conceded a league-high average of 14.1 points to opposing tight ends in 2025 and aren't looking any better this year after getting torched by Dalton Schultz (12/140/0 on 14 targets) in Week 2. Freiermuth was the TE3 in his first matchup with Cincy last year—going off for 111 yards and two touchdowns—and has real potential to light this defense up again in 2026.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams make NFL history in Rams’ blowout win over Giants
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford and Davante Adams combined for a memorable performance as the Rams overwhelmed the Giants without Puka Nacua.
articles.body:
Matthew Stafford and Davante Adams did not merely help the Los Angeles Rams earn their first victory of the season Monday night. They continued climbing two of the NFL's most exclusive career lists.

Stafford passed Philip Rivers for sixth place in league history in career touchdown passes, while Adams moved within two receiving touchdowns of Larry Fitzgerald as the Rams defeated the New York Giants 28-6 at SoFi Stadium.

Stafford completed 22 of 31 passes for 327 yards, four touchdowns and one interception. It was the 22nd game of his career with at least four touchdown passes. Adams caught eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns despite receiving added attention with Puka Nacua unavailable because of a hip and groin injury.

The performance was exactly what Los Angeles needed after opening its season with a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Stafford and Adams take over without Nacua

The Rams entered Monday night without Nacua or Jordan Whittington , leaving Adams as the obvious focal point of the passing game. The Giants still could not stop him.

Stafford connected with Adams for a 31-yard touchdown with 11 seconds remaining in the first quarter. The two veterans struck again on an 11-yard score during the third quarter, giving Adams 119 career receiving touchdowns. Fitzgerald ranks sixth in NFL history with 121. Adams is now positioned to pass one of the greatest receivers ever if he maintains his early-season pace.

Stafford's four touchdown passes increased his career total to 427. He entered the game tied with Rivers at 425 before moving ahead of him.

Kyren Williams and rookie tight end Terrance Ferguson caught Stafford's other two touchdown passes. Los Angeles finished with 439 total yards despite the absence of its leading receiver from last season. Adams accounted for nearly 60 percent of Stafford's passing yardage.

Rams face quick turnaround before Week 3 test

The Rams will have little time to enjoy their first win. Los Angeles travels to Denver for a Sunday night matchup against the Broncos in Week 3. Nacua's availability will be one of the most important developments to monitor throughout the week.

His return would give Stafford two elite targets against a Denver defense that is far more dangerous than the depleted unit Los Angeles faced Monday. The Rams also will want to clean up their two turnovers. Jevon Holland intercepted Stafford and forced a Williams fumble, creating New York's only meaningful opportunities.

The mistakes did not affect the result against the Giants. They could prove much more costly against a stronger opponent.

Still, Monday's performance showed why the Rams remain a legitimate NFC contender. Stafford can continue producing at an elite level, Adams remains capable of taking over a game and Sean McVay's offense can adapt when an important player is unavailable.

Los Angeles entered Monday night needing a response after an ugly opener. Stafford and Adams provided a historic one.

articles.title: One ex-NFL star thinks Harry Kane could make transition to American football
articles.summary: FC Bayern’s Harry Kane to the NFL? Maybe…
articles.body:
Harry Kane has conquered just about every challenge football has thrown at him, so perhaps it is time for the Bayern Munich striker to try something completely different — the NFL.

Former Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars linebacker Paul Posluszny believes Kane could actually make the transition from football to American football, although he has a very specific career path in mind.

According to Posluszny. a Pennsylvania schoolboy legend, Kane could potentially handle punting or kickoffs thanks to his powerful leg.

"I think if Harry Kane has that powerful leg, he can dedicate some time to kickoffs. Field goals and extra points will be the challenging ones. Now you get him out there as the punter or leading the kickoff team, that's all about strength, power, and putting the ball where it needs to go, which is all things that he is completely accustomed to. So, he would be able to make the transition," Posluszny told iPredicta .

Imagine Kane spending Sunday afternoons at the Allianz Arena scoring goals and then somehow turning up in Buffalo on Monday wearing a helmet.

There would probably be a learning curve. NFL punters have spent years perfecting a completely different technique, and Kane might have a few questions about why everyone keeps trying to tackle him.

Still, there is something hilarious about the idea of Kane being told that after years of mastering the beautiful game, his next challenge is to stand around waiting for someone to yell "PUNT!"

And knowing Kane, he would probably find a way to score anyway.

articles.title: Rams' Aaron Donald Says He's 'A Little Sore' After Return from NFL Retirement vs. Giants
articles.summary: After playing his first NFL game in 32 months on Monday night, Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of it feeling okay all things considered.
articles.body:
After playing his first NFL game in 32 months on Monday night, Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of it feeling okay all things considered.

Speaking to reporters following the Rams' 28-6 win over the New York Giants, Donald said he was "a little sore" right now coming off of "two panicked practices and then a game."

Donald also had a wrap on his right hand after the game, but also described that as "just a little sore."

Donald retired in March 2024 after a 10-year career, but he decided to give it a go once again on Aug. 30 when he signed a one-year deal to return to the Rams.

After sitting out Los Angeles' Week 1 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers in Australia to continue ramping up, Donald was in the starting lineup on Monday night. He recorded three total tackles and one tackle for loss in 32 snaps against the Giants.

New York's game plan was focused, at least in part, on ensuring Donald didn't wreck things because he was double-teamed on seven of his 32 snaps.

The Rams needed the boost Donald provided with Myles Garrett on injured reserve after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery. The Giants' 182 yards of offense were the fewest allowed in a game by Los Angeles since Week 1 of the 2023 season against the Seattle Seahawks (180).

Things figure to get more difficult for Donald and the Rams over the next three weeks. Their upcoming schedule includes road games against the Denver Broncos and Philadelphia Eagles before returning home to host the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5.

articles.title: Tom Brady, Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders' surprise start to the NFL season
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL presenter Neil Reynolds explores the early impact of Kirk Cousins in leading the Las Vegas Raiders to a surprise unbeaten start through the first two weeks of the season; Cousins starred in Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers as he plays mentor to Fernando Mendoza
articles.body:
As many of you know, the seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback has a top front office job with the Raiders, as well as being a TV commentator, and it's his job to try to build the silver and black back into a contender. But they felt miles away from contention on that night in November.

They'd just lost 33-16 to the Cowboys, Geno Smith was ineffective a quarterback and arguing with fans in the stands, star defensive end Max Crosby was so frustrated at the final gun that he launched his helmet about 40 yards across the field.

That stadium in Las Vegas is nicknamed the Death Star, and as I walked away that night, I was reminded of the very first Star Wars film and thought, like the original Death Star, this thing needs to be blown up. Not the stadium, but the football program.

Head coach Pete Carroll was in the final throes of his potentially Hall of Fame career, and it's kind of fitting that he was in Las Vegas. It's the place where legendary names go to sell tickets, and I felt like that was what was happening there with the Raiders last year with Pete Carroll at the helm.

But this team is now laying down what seem to be proper foundations. They had the first overall pick in the NFL draft, and they used it well with the obvious selection of Fernando Mendoza out of Indiana.

And then you think, well, that means they're going to throw him into the fire straight away. That's been the way it's been done in the NFL in recent years. There aren't many teams that take a patient approach anymore.

Rookie quarterbacks are thrown to the wolves occasionally. Look at Cam Ward last year with the Tennessee Titans. Beaten from start to finish of the season, then spends the first part of the offseason rehabbing a shoulder injury that he suffered in Week 18.

The last really patient approach of quarterback that was notable was probably the Kansas City Chiefs resisting the temptation to put Patrick Mahomes in as a rookie, having him sit and learn for a year under an unselfish proven veteran in Alex Smith. And the Raiders have replicated that model, and so far it's worked.

They brought in Kirk Cousins, and the relationship between Cousins and Mendoza is not only endearing and quirky, it's also going to be very valuable. Cousins will have some limitations as a quarterback, but he is a safe pair of hands, and he knows how to get you in and out of the huddle. He knows how to win games.

Even this past week, as the Raiders moved to 2-0 on the season, you saw some of the veteran smarts that are going to help the Silver and Black this year.

On one of his touchdown passes against the Chargers, pre-snap, Cousins was constantly looking behind, signaling to the running back time and time again. Now yes, he could have been calling out protections, but it's also a good chance he was trying to pull the defense into thinking a running play was coming, and then he tosses the ball into the end zone for a touchdown.

So the Raiders are 2-0, one of the surprising teams to be with that record in the early stages of this season, and they can now really take their time in bringing Mendoza along. I spoke to Cousins in the summer, and he talked about why he was excited for this opportunity in Las Vegas, and I got the impression it was because this is his job for this year if things go well.

I could see a scenario where we have a wire-to-wire Cousins situation with the Raiders, and how he works with Klint Kubiak, the new head coach, he's got it all laid out before him. It's going to be fascinating to see.

The thing with Kirk as well is he's one of the most unselfish and nicest guys in the NFL. So even if it's to his long-term detriment, he is going to bring Mendoza along. He is not going to close himself off in the quarterback room. He's never going to keep secrets and tips and advice to himself.

He will be an extra coach in effect for their franchise quarterback in waiting. So it feels like there's a newer approach with the Raiders, a more patient approach.

I think Kubiak has time now to build the program the right way. He's got young players who he can work with for many years. Ashton Jeanty at running back, Brock Bowers at tight end. If they can keep Maxx Crosby healthy and productive on the other side of the ball, then there are pieces in place.

But the most important piece for the Raiders this season is a quarterback that very few teams around the NFL wanted anymore, and that's Kirk Cousins. He has a mighty role to play for the Silver and Black this season, but how he operates in the coming months could set the stage for this team to be competitive in many, many years to come.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Injury Update, New Timeline to Return for Rams After Missing Week 2 vs. Giants
articles.summary: After missing the Los Angeles Rams' 28-6 win over the New York Giants on Monday Night Football in Week 2, star wide receiver Puka Nacua's status for Week 3 isn't yet clear.
articles.body:
After missing the Los Angeles Rams' 28-6 win over the New York Giants on Monday Night Football in Week 2, star wide receiver Puka Nacua's status for Week 3 isn't yet clear.

According to ESPN's Sarah Barshop , Rams head coach Sean McVay said he's "hopeful" Nacua will be back but stopped short of providing a definitive expectation.

Nacua was inactive for Monday's win after being added to the Rams' injury report on Friday with a hip ailment.

Leading up to Monday's game, McVay told reporters Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin, and that he "didn't feel totally like himself" during Thursday's practice.

Nacua was nagged by a psoas (core muscle) injury during training camp, but McVay noted that the injury that caused his star wideout to miss Week 2 was unrelated.

The 25-year-old Nacua entered 2026 coming off the best season of his young NFL career.

He set career highs across the board in 2025 with 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, resulting in Pro Bowl and First Team All-Pro honors, and a third-place finish in the NFL Offensive Player of the Year voting.

In the Rams' 2026 season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Nacua was one of the team's few effective players on offense, finishing with five catches for 74 yards.

Without Nacua in the lineup on Monday, the offense funneled almost entirely through veteran wideout Davante Adams, who had eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns with reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford throwing him the ball.

If Nacua is unable to play again in Week 3, Adams should remain Stafford's top target with running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, and tight end Terrance Ferguson playing pivotal roles as well.

articles.title: 5 Contracts NFL Teams Already Regret 2 Weeks Into 2026 Season
articles.summary: Less than a month into the 2026 NFL season, it's already becoming painfully apparent that several of the blockbuster contracts players agreed to during the latest free-agency signing period are going to be massive busts.
articles.body:
Less than a month into the 2026 NFL season, it's already becoming painfully apparent that several of the blockbuster contracts players agreed to during the latest free-agency signing period are going to be massive busts.

There are major red flags surrounding some of the league's highest-paid players who have now had bad games in back-to-back weeks. While sluggish Week 1 showings are to be expected and can be overcome, two consecutive poor performances are indicative of a trend. Teams now have cause to be genuinely concerned about the pricy investments they made into these disappointing players.

With that in mind, let's highlight five contracts that already look regrettable before Week 3 even kicks off.

Contract Extension: Three Years, $165 Million ($120 Million Guaranteed)

After a back-and-forth contractual saga played out throughout the bulk of the 2026 offseason, the stalemate between Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally ended with the quarterback signing the richest deal in franchise history.

When he inked a three-year, $165 million extension with $120 million in new guaranteed money, Mayfield not only became the league's third-highest paid quarterback, but set the bar extremely high for himself going into the 2026 season.

Despite being compensated as one of the NFL's best at his position, Mayfield hasn't played anywhere close to a top-five level through the first two weeks of the campaign.

While he's completing 71 percent of his throws, Mayfield is averaging a career-low 6.4 yards per attempt and has recorded just one touchdown pass. He's turned the ball over four times and taken seven sacks, a large reason why the Bucs are off to an 0-2 start and are already in real danger of missing the playoffs for the second consecutive year.

Although Mayfield was initially a revelation for a Tampa franchise that looked lost in wake of Tom Brady's retirement after the 2022 campaign, he's dropped off noticeably since stringing together Pro Bowl campaigns in 2023-24.

Mayfield may have reached his zenith during his most recent Pro Bowl season, having posted career highs of 4,500 passing yards and 41 passing touchdowns on a 71.4 percent completion percentage. His production dipped to a far more pedestrian 63.2 percent completion rate, 3,693 passing yards and 26 passing touchdowns in 2025.

Given the poor start, Mayfield doesn't appear to be anywhere close to returning to his 2024 form and may never reach that peak again.

Although Mayfield is still a competent passer who could conceivably oversee an offense just good enough to reach the playoffs, he's not elevating the Bucs to a Super Bowl level. If he can't lock in and improve his numbers significantly while guiding Tampa to some desperately needed wins to close out September, the organization will rue its decision to re-up Mayfield at such a high price.

RB Travis Etienne Jr., New Orleans Saints

Free-Agent Contract: Four Years, $48 Million ($28 Million Guaranteed)

It's become a risky endeavor to dole out a second contracts NFL running backs, with Travis Etienne Jr. becoming the latest star rusher to regress after inking a new deal in free agency.

Etienne, a first-round pick by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2021 draft, earned a sizable contract from the New Orleans Saints in free agency after his bounce-back 2025 campaign. Etienne shook off injuries and poor play the season before to put up 1,399 yards and a career-high 13 touchdowns from scrimmage.

While Etienne was an important piece of Jacksonville's offense during a resurgent 13-4 season, it was telling that the club didn't make a strong push to retain him. The decision to let the 27-year-old walk in free agency now looks to be a shrewd one, as Etienne has only put up 71 rushing yards on 17 totes and hasn't made a single trip to the end zone in 2026.

Etienne did do some heavy lifting as a pass-catcher in New Orleans' opener—securing seven of his nine targets for 32 yards—but was far less a factor in his squad's Week 2 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The veteran finished the game with a meager 31 yards from scrimmage on 10 touches.

To make matters worse, Alvin Kamara made his 2026 debut against Baltimore and cut into Etienne's workload significantly.

Although Kamara only mustered 15 yards on his nine totes and took his five catches for a meager seven yards, the fading 31-year-old logged 20 offensive snaps in the contest—a major reason why Etienne's snap count dropped from 53 in Week 1 to 37 this past weekend. Third-stringer CJ Donaldson has also been more involved than originally expected, getting on the field for 22.2 percent of New Orleans' offensive snaps over the first two weeks.

Considering Etienne is being paid as an upper-echelon running back, the Saints need far better returns in the coming weeks before this contract winds up being a significant albatross on their books.

Contract Extension: Four Years, $114 Million ($84 Million Gauranteed)

The Indianapolis Colts rewarded Alec Pierce with a huge contract extensions following the 2025 season as part of their push to keep the key pieces from last year's lineup together. The cash-strapped club elected to prioritize retaining the players who helped Indy jump out to a 7-1 start during the first half of the season, ignoring the fact that injuries ravaged the roster and led the Colts to finish outside the playoffs with an 8-9 record.

While a 47-catch, 1,003-receiving yard season proved that Pierce can work as a needle-moving, field-stretching wideout, a nagging heel injury has largely kept the 26-year-old from reaching his ceiling in the NFL.

Pierce first picked up the heel ailment late in 2024 and it continued to bother him throughout the 2025 campaign. He attempted to treat the issue with a platelet-rich plasma injection early in the offseason before opting for surgery this past March.

Although Pierce returned in time for the start of the 2026 campaign and played relatively well in the opener (catching four of his six targets for 61 yards), head coach Shane Steichen confirmed that the team's top wideout aggravated the heel early in Week 2. Pierce is now slated to miss extensive time as he rehabilitates the injury yet again.

While Pierce is hoping to avoid surgery this time around, Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network revealed that a procedure isn't off the table and an IR stint could be in the cards regardless.

It was already going to be difficult for Pierce to live up to his nine-figure extension without the heel injury flaring up. With the injury already causing him to miss a chunk of time and potentially limiting him upon his return, it will be near-impossible for Pierce to perform at the level expected of one of the league's top-15 highest-paid receivers.

Things look bleak for a Colts team that already lacked depth in the receiving corps after parting ways with Michael Pittman Jr. this offseason. Pierce's absence could doom the team to another postseason-less campaign and make the front office deeply regret investing in an extension.

Free-Agent Contract: Four Years, $70 million ($38 Million Gauranteed)

Wan'Dale Robinson established himself as one of the NFL's top possession receivers during the latter half of his four-year tenure with the New York Giants. Robinson parlayed his immense slot talents into a blockbuster contract offer from the Tennessee Titans this offseason.

After two weeks of play, it doesn't seem that either side is benefitting from the new arrangement.

Robinson was supposed to be a safety valve for up-and-coming quarterback Cam Ward, but the pair can't seem to get on the same page. The battery has only hooked up six times on the season, generating a meager 47 yards and zero touchdowns in a pair of defeats.

It's a far cry from the prolific production Robinson had under current offensive coordinator Brian Daboll, who selected the wideout in the second round of the 2022 draft during his tenure as Big Blue's head coach. Robinson steadily improved each season, culminating in a breakout 2025 season in which he recorded 92 catches on 140 targets for 1,014 yards and four touchdowns.

While it Robinson looked like he could be on his way to another impressive statistical season after tallying five catches on six targets in his Titans debut, that performance was followed by a highly-concerning one-catch, one-target outing against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Considering Robinson was only held to a single catch or fewer once over his final 33 games with the G-Men and logged multiple targets in each of those contests, it's obvious that there is a glaring lack of rapport between Robinson and Ward right now.

Although Robinson is currently tied with Elic Ayomanor and tight end Gunnar Helm for the second-most targets on the team behind top weapon Carnell Tate, the wideout has hardly produced more than running back Tyjae Spears (four catches for 41 yards on six targets).

These are unacceptable marks for a wideout who is being paid handsomely to move the chains and rack up a high volume of catches in Tennessee's offensive system. If Robinson can't get on the same page as Ward, his contract will be one the Titans quickly come to regret.

Contract Extension: Three Years, $54 Million ($36 Million Guaranteed)

Kyle Pitts Sr. has had a polarizing start to his NFL career, one that began with him becoming the highest drafted tight end in history at No. 4 overall in the 2021 draft. Injuries and inconsistency plagued Pitts for the better part of the past half-decade, but he finally put things together in 2025 to record some of the best statistical marks of his career.

With Pitts fresh off an 88-catch, 928-yard, five-touchdown campaign, the Falcons rewarded his steady production with a contract extension that made him the NFL's fourth-highest paid player at the tight end position.

That decision is looking extremely regrettable after Pitts managed just one catch for 15 yards over the first two games of the 2026 NFL season.

Pitts has been a non-factor in Atlanta's league-worst passing attack, generating a woeful four targets during the team's two losses. A good portion of the blame for this lack of production can be placed on veteran third-stringer Cooper Rush and undrafted free agent rookie Jack Strand—who have unexpectedly filled in for injured QBs Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. to open the 2026 campaign—but Pitts hasn't appeared to be giving his best efforts either.

Fortunately for Pitts, Penix is slated to return to action in Week 3. That quarterback change will give Pitts and the rest of Atlanta's slumping offense a fair chance to turn things around after a truly dreadful start. If Pitts can't figure things out with Penix under center, Atlanta will be saddled with one of the league's worst contracts.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s Snap Count Spotlighted After Giants' Loss to Rams Amid Malik Nabers Injury
articles.summary: Even though Malik Nabers was able to return in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams after suffering a shoulder injury in the first quarter, at least one New York Giants analyst put the spotlight on Odell Beckham Jr.'s lack of reps in the game.
articles.body:
Even though Malik Nabers was able to return in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams after suffering a shoulder injury in the first quarter, at least one New York Giants analyst put the spotlight on Odell Beckham Jr.'s lack of reps in the game.

Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News noted Beckham only played three snaps in the game, despite having "strong" chemistry with backup quarterback Jameis Winston in training camp and preseason.

Nabers told reporters after the game he "just popped" his shoulder back into place. He was back on the field for New York's next possession.

Winston entered on the Giants' second offensive possession after Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury on a third-down incompletion that ended the opening drive.

The offense had nothing going against the Rams with Winston at quarterback. They had 182 yards of offense, 11 first downs and went a combined 4-of-16 on third- and fourth-down.

As for Beckham's role, he was always unlikely to get significant playing time barring injuries after being a potential cut candidate before the Giants opted to keep him on the 53-man roster coming out of camp.

Nabers' injury initially seemed like it might be significant, but he was back on the field almost immediately. Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields are ahead of Beckham on the depth chart. Tight end Isaiah Likely leads the team in targets (18), receptions (13) and receiving yards (111).

Beckham, who is 33 and didn't play during the 2025 season, has not been targeted in 14 offensive snaps played through the first two games for the Giants.

There may come a point when Beckham gets a bigger role for head coach John Harbaugh, but the offense has more important things to figure out right now with Dart expected to miss some time with what is believed to be a sprained MCL.
